audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in the François 2005 text we hold layer at the stated sections. (2) The record rests on a 2005 historical-comparative article, but that is the best there is: Glottolog, HAL and François's own publication list show no grammar, grammar sketch (beyond Codrington 1885, which I re-read and which has no accent statement) or phonology of Lo-Toga; the explicit last-non-schwa-vowel rule is published for the sister language Hiw only. Three further François items downloaded now (2007 noun articles; Krauße & François 2023, 2024) are silent on Lo-Toga word-stress placement, as is the online dictionary. (3) The not determinable coding is therefore correct and cannot be improved from published sources; the only refinement worth adding to the prose rule is François 2005 sec. 5.1.1 ('Hiu and Lo-Toga.. tend to centralize any vowel that does not receive primary stress') alongside the a

sources.note: No published synchronic stress statement exists for Lo-Toga; the only route past not determinable is an in-house acoustic check of whether stress falls on the last full (non-schwa) vowel as in Hiw (François 2010) -- the open Pangloss audio is the material for that. Not a citable description, so low priority.
